attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter, written in the first person, and restated as his prediction in August 2024.

semantics.note: 'I believe … will', later called 'my prediction', is a scored forecast. But the words give AI three quarters before the 'apocalypse', and the revenue savaging comes 'when it does'. So the savaging follows the deadline. The draft puts the savaging itself inside the three quarters, which says more than he did.

contract.note: The contract tests revenue for the quarter ending 2024-12-31, the last quarter before the apocalypse would arrive. Revenue lags, so any savaging would show up only in later quarters. Treating Q4 2024 revenue as the test is the contract's choice, not something the speaker supplied. The result depends on that choice.

evidence.note: Microsoft's own disclosure, correctly dated: revenue for the quarter ended 2024-12-31 was up 12%. That quarter is the end of the 'prove itself' window, not the period after the apocalypse when savaging was forecast, so it does not settle the outcome.
Alphabet's own disclosure, correctly dated: Q4 2024 revenue was up 12%. Same timing problem as Microsoft. It shows no collapse by year end but says nothing about the quarters that followed.
Zitron's 2026 admission that he 'goofed'. It shows how he reads his own claim, but the speaker's own statements cannot resolve the outcome.

output.rationale: The three-quarter window has passed. Microsoft and Alphabet both grew revenue 12% in Q4 2024, so there was no collapse by year end. But the forecast puts the revenue savaging after the apocalypse, which was due at the end of the window. Testing Q4 2024 revenue is the contract's own reading. The packet has no 2025 revenue and no Amazon figures, and his later admission cannot resolve the claim. On the evidence given, the outcome is not settled.
